todays_decisions.reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's risk-off call (confidence 0.55). SPY is 0.36% above its 200-day, realized vol is 23.3% against 13.8%, VIXY is rising, bonds and gold are falling with stocks, and the Nvidia reaction is not in the packet. I rejected the only proposal, selling half of VTI. L9 says to state the shared-stop weight and size VOO and VTI as one position: they are about 23.5% of equity on one SPY 200-day line, and both stop blocks read NEAR at +0.4%. That stop already sells the whole group on one close below 729.79, and I keep the 11-17 pre-commitment to let it sell both together. The Skeptic's serious timing objection holds. Selling half now only saves the overshoot past the line on the day it trips. It sells after a 2.3% five-day drop, which is where the Market Analyst says his call most often fails, and it reverses the 11-16 add after two sessions. The Implicator is also right that about $0.71 of the loss would be wash-sale disallowed against the 11-16 lot, so the 'harvest' claim is wrong. The direction thesis (VTI lags SPY) runs against the 21-day data (VTI -4.09% vs SPY -4.44%). L8: the Market Analyst says 'do not add', not 'sell', and VTI's stored text already says no adds, so there is no contradiction to fix there. No buys were proposed. Cash is about 11.5%, roughly $9 over the 10% buffer, so the owner's 'mostly invested' goal is close to met. My reasons for not deploying more today are WMT's company-confirmed 11-19 print, Staples already at 16.5% by bucket and the risk-off stance, not L4. Holdings check (L7) from the stop blocks: no price stop has tripped, and VOO/VTI are NEAR. Qualitative clauses: VOO/VTI RSP 21d is +1.11%, still positive but fading, so untripped, and VTI's $345.20 cost clause is not hit. WMT: XLP 21d is still above +3%, and there is no guidance cut because the print is tomorrow. I follow the News Analyst in reading the 11-17 'Reports Q3' headline as a mis-summarized preview, since there is no 8-K 2.02. KR: the cyber incident is unconfirmed and the 12-03 print has not happened. INCY: the $1.29M insider sale is sentiment, there is no guidance-cut or trial-failure 8-K, and MAESTRA-3 was already judged. EXEL: no 8-K, still on the menu, 5.4% above its stop and the closest single name after MCO. IDXX, CARG, MSCI, VRSN and DPZ: no guidance cut, reversal or negative 8-K. DPZ is still on the menu with CFO above net income. FAST: no cash-flow miss. MCO and SAM are still on the menu. Holdings review: I disagree with the VTI trim for the reasons above. The Skeptic's VOO alternative is not a proposal, and its claim that VOO would harvest cleanly is wrong: the 10-23 and 10-26 VOO lots fall within 30 days. I accept the WMT hold but take the Skeptic's point that a close-based stop does not protect against a gap. The one-third 11-13 trim is the sizing for that, and no further trim was proposed. On MCO the Skeptic is right under L8: the stored premise (Financials favored) is gone from today's note. I restate its thesis on quality and low beta and name it the first sell candidate for the next run. I keep the $470 stop (3.07% above) rather than selling on a premise the Proposer did not turn into a trade. I accept the FAST and CARG holds as low-beta quality held against the 'avoid' tilts, with no adds. Thesis updates (L6): I re-dated the SPY 200-day to 729.79 (11-17 close) for VOO and VTI, and restated SAM's $201 stop from its $220.14 fill (about 8.7% under it, not 10%). L2 shaped no sizing today because there were no buys; every held name's next date was checked from filings by the News Analyst.

rejected.why: The stored SPY 200-day stop already sells all of VOO and VTI one close lower, so trimming half now only saves the overshoot. It sells into a 2.3% drop right before the Nvidia reaction is known (the Skeptic's serious timing objection). It reverses a two-session-old add with about $0.71 of the loss wash-sale disallowed (Implicator). And its 'VTI lags SPY' thesis runs against the 21-day data. The Implicator's lower stress figure is real but small next to that, and the shared stop is the plan.
